key_insight: Scal3R applies scalable test-time training to feed-forward 3D reconstruction models so they can adapt online to very long video sequences by summarizing global context in a memory-efficient way, substantially improving long-range accuracy and consistency.
problem_solved: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models lose accuracy and produce inconsistent geometry over long video sequences because they lack mechanisms to capture global context and are constrained by limited memory during inference.
method: Online test-time training: adapt model weights per sequence at inference time to fit scene-specific cues without full offline retraining.
Compact global context memory: maintain a bounded, low-cost scene summary (scene embeddings / buffer) that aggregates long-range information for consistency across frames.
Lightweight geometric & temporal consistency objectives: use efficient loss terms and localized optimization to enforce coherent reconstructions while keeping compute and memory low.
impact: Enables reliable large-scale 3D reconstruction from long videos by improving fidelity and temporal consistency without prohibitive memory or retraining costs, facilitating robust mapping, AR, and robotics applications in real-world deployments.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: video frames → feed-forward reconstructor → test-time training module ↔ compact scene memory → final 3D mesh/point cloud
Before/after comparison: reconstruction quality and temporal consistency for long sequences (baseline vs Scal3R)
Performance chart: reconstruction accuracy versus sequence length showing Scal3R maintaining accuracy as length grows
Resource plot: memory and latency vs baseline, illustrating bounded overhead of the compact memory approach
paper_title: Scal3R: Scalable Test-Time Training for Large-Scale 3D Reconstruction
paper_authors: Tao Xie, Peishan Yang, Yudong Jin, Yingfeng Cai, Wei Yin
